nodes.label: Coverage is broad, not a two-engine spot check: 306 models carry all five eng...
nodes.statement: Coverage is broad, not a two-engine spot check: 306 models carry all five engines and 725 carry four or more. Per-engine reach is uneven — tellurium 985, amici 879, copasi 870, pysces 770, simbio 367 — so simbio is the coverage-limiting engine, not a correctness-limiting one.

nodes.label: This study measures COVERAGE, not scored trajectory agreement. Whether the ov...
nodes.statement: This study measures COVERAGE, not scored trajectory agreement. Whether the overlapping engines actually agree per-model is inspectable in the corpus explorer and quantified on the BIOMD1-3 subset by the repeat-matching study (exact agreement where observables are computed). The corpus-wide agreement claim is therefore scoped — supported by the subset result plus per-model explorability, not yet a corpus-wide scored number.

nodes.statement: After the iteration-2 coverage fix, every repeat arm reproduces the BioSimulators reference exactly: 12/12 arms have matched == total under numpy allclose, with zero numerical mismatches.

nodes.label: The residual failures are coverage, not numerics: iteration 1 left 17/48 refe...
nodes.statement: The residual failures are coverage, not numerics: iteration 1 left 17/48 reference observables uncomputed on BIOMD1-2; iteration 2 closed that to 0 there and 2 on BIOMD3 (SED-ML dataGenerator forms not yet supported). This confirms the hypothesis that the dominant failure mode is missing observables rather than divergent trajectories.

nodes.label: Cross-engine reproducibility is exact where observables overlap: 22/30 iter2 ...
nodes.statement: Cross-engine reproducibility is exact where observables overlap: 22/30 iter2 pairs match fully. The 8 residuals are understood — pysces computes 2/65 observables differently from copasi/tellurium/amici on BIOMD1, and simbio exposes a reduced 48-observable set (those 48 all agree). simbio, the new engine, lands on the engines that already agree.
